q: The maximum amount of Leave on Average Pay (LAP) that can be availed of at a time by a railway servant is:
e: Leave on Average Pay can be availed in one spell up to a maximum of 180 days at a time; any absence beyond this requires combination with another kind of leave.

q: Child Care Leave can be granted to a female railway employee for a maximum period of:
e: Child Care Leave is admissible to a female railway servant for a maximum of 730 days during her entire service, for taking care of her two eldest surviving children.

q: Under the National Pension System (NPS), the Government's contribution for a railway employee is:
e: Under the National Pension System, the Government contributes 14% of Basic Pay plus DA for railway employees, while the employee's own contribution is 10%.

q: The ceiling on Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity (DCRG) under the 7th CPC dispensation is:
e: The maximum gratuity (retirement/death gratuity) is now Rs 25 lakh. (Source: DoPPW OM No. 28/03/2024-P&PW(B)/Gratuity/9559 dated 30.05.2024; Railway Board RBE No. 50/2024 dated 31.05.2024; effective 01.01.2024.)

q: Composite Transfer Grant (CTG) payable on retirement is:

options.A: 100% of last Basic Pay in all cases
options.B: 80% of last Basic Pay, irrespective of distance

e: Composite Transfer Grant payable on retirement is 80% of the last Basic Pay drawn, irrespective of the distance involved in the transfer.

q: Maternity leave admissible to a female railway employee (with less than two surviving children) is:
e: A female railway employee with less than two surviving children is entitled to maternity leave of 180 days, which is not debited to her leave account.

q: Paternity leave admissible to a male railway employee with less than two surviving children is:
e: Paternity leave of 15 days is admissible to a male railway employee with less than two surviving children, to be availed around the confinement of his wife.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Suspension is a penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules.
2. A railway servant under suspension is entitled to subsistence allowance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: suspension is not a penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules; it is only an interim measure. Statement 2 is true: a suspended servant is paid subsistence allowance, so 2 only is correct.

q: The minimum pension admissible to a retired railway employee under the 7th CPC dispensation is:
e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, the minimum pension admissible is Rs 9,000 per month, exclusive of dearness relief admissible thereon.

q: The ceiling for House Building Advance (HBA) is:

options.A: 100 times Basic Pay or Rs 50 lakh, whichever is less
options.B: 139 times Basic Pay or Rs 1 crore, whichever is less
options.C: 120 times Basic Pay or Rs 75 lakh, whichever is less
options.D: 150 times Basic Pay or Rs 1.5 crore, whichever is less

e: House Building Advance is limited to 139 times the Basic Pay or Rs 1 crore, whichever is less, and is further restricted to the actual cost of the house.

q: The maximum amount of Leave on Average Pay (LAP) that a railway servant can accumulate at his credit is:
e: Leave on Average Pay can accumulate only up to a maximum of 300 days at credit; LAP earned beyond this ceiling is not carried forward.

q: Leave on Average Pay is earned by a railway servant at the rate of:

options.A: 2 days for each completed month of service
options.B: 2 and a half days for each completed month of service
options.C: 3 days for each completed month of service
options.D: 1 day for each completed month of service

e: Leave on Average Pay is earned at the rate of 2 and a half days for each completed month of service, i.e., 30 days in a year, credited in two instalments of 15 days each.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Leave on Half Average Pay (LHAP) is admissible at the rate of 20 days for each completed year of service.
2. There is no maximum limit for accumulation of LHAP.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: LHAP accrues at 20 days for each completed year of service, and unlike LAP it has no maximum limit on accumulation.

q: 'Leave Not Due' is granted to a railway servant:

options.A: In advance of the LAP at his credit, without any condition
options.B: On medical certificate, when no LHAP is at his credit, and is debited against the LHAP he will earn in future

e: Leave Not Due is granted on medical certificate when no LHAP is at the servant's credit, and it is debited against the LHAP that he will earn in future.

q: Extra Ordinary Leave (EOL) is characterised by the fact that:

options.A: Full leave salary is payable during the leave
options.B: Half leave salary is payable during the leave
options.C: No leave salary is payable during the leave
options.D: It can be granted only on medical grounds

e: Extra Ordinary Leave carries no leave salary at all; it is granted when no other leave is admissible or in the special circumstances specified in the rules.

q: When Leave on Half Average Pay is commuted into commuted leave on medical certificate, the leave account is debited with:

options.A: The same number of days as the commuted leave granted
options.B: Twice the number of days of commuted leave granted
options.C: Half the number of days of commuted leave granted

e: Commuted leave is the conversion of LHAP into leave on full average pay; hence the leave account is debited with twice the number of days of commuted leave granted.

q: Study leave may ordinarily be granted to a railway servant up to a maximum of:

options.B: 24 months, extendable to 36 months in specified cases

e: Study leave may ordinarily be granted up to a maximum of 24 months, which may be extended to 36 months in specified cases such as certain specialised courses.

q: On the death of a railway servant in service, his family may be permitted to retain the railway quarter for a period up to:
e: On the death of a railway servant in service, his family may be permitted to retain the railway quarter for a period up to 24 months at normal rent.

q: 'Stepping up' of pay refers to:

options.A: Grant of an advance increment for good work
options.B: Bringing the pay of a senior employee at par with that of his junior where the junior, due to fixation of pay, draws more pay than the senior
options.C: Fixation of pay at the minimum of the pay scale

e: Stepping up removes a pay anomaly: where a junior, due to fixation of pay on promotion, draws more pay than his senior, the senior's pay is brought at par with the junior's, subject to the prescribed conditions.

q: The Next Below Rule (NBR) is applied in pay fixation to:

options.A: Fix the pay of an employee at the stage next below his present pay
options.B: Allow proforma fixation/promotion benefit to an employee who is away from his parent cadre (e.g., on deputation or ex-cadre post) when his next below (junior) in the parent cadre gets promoted
options.C: Protect the pay of the junior-most employee in a cadre
options.D: Compute the pay of an employee under suspension

e: The Next Below Rule allows proforma fixation and promotion benefit to an employee who is away from his parent cadre on deputation or an ex-cadre post when his junior in the parent cadre is promoted.

q: Under the Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) scheme, financial upgradations are admissible on completion of:
e: Under the Modified Assured Career Progression scheme, three financial upgradations are admissible on completion of 10, 20 and 30 years of service to employees who do not get regular promotions.

q: Which of the following is a major penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules?

options.D: Recovery from pay of pecuniary loss caused

e: Removal from service is a major penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules; censure, withholding of passes and recovery from pay of pecuniary loss are minor penalties.

q: The distinction between 'removal from service' and 'dismissal from service' is that:

options.A: There is no distinction between the two
options.B: Dismissal ordinarily debars the employee from future employment under the Government, whereas removal does not by itself entail such disqualification
options.C: Removal is a minor penalty while dismissal is a major penalty
options.D: Removal is applicable only to gazetted staff

e: Dismissal from service ordinarily debars the employee from future employment under the Government, whereas removal from service does not by itself entail such disqualification.

q: A railway servant who remains under police custody for a period exceeding 48 hours is:

options.B: Deemed to have been placed under suspension from the date of his detention

e: A railway servant who remains under police custody for a period exceeding 48 hours is deemed to have been placed under suspension from the date of his detention.

q: Subsistence allowance payable to a railway servant under suspension is generally equal to:

options.A: The full pay he was drawing
options.B: The leave salary which he would have drawn on half average pay (i.e., 50% of pay), plus dearness allowance admissible thereon
options.D: A fixed amount of Rs 5,000 per month

e: Subsistence allowance during suspension is equal to the leave salary which the servant would have drawn on half average pay, i.e., 50% of pay, plus dearness allowance admissible thereon.

q: Under the National Pension System, PRAN allotted to a subscriber stands for:
e: PRAN stands for Permanent Retirement Account Number, the unique and portable account number allotted to every subscriber under the National Pension System.

q: A retired railway employee can commute for a lump sum payment a maximum of:
e: A retired railway employee can commute for a lump sum payment a maximum of 40% of his pension; the balance pension continues to be paid monthly.

q: 'Fee' differs from 'honorarium' in that a fee is:

options.B: A payment received from a source other than the general revenues of the Government

e: A fee is a recurring or non-recurring payment received by a Government servant from a source other than the general revenues of the Government, whereas honorarium is paid out of the general revenues for special work.

q: Posts on the Railways which are filled on the basis of a positive act of selection (merit) are called:
e: Posts which are filled on the basis of a positive act of selection on merit are called selection posts, as distinct from non-selection posts filled by seniority subject to rejection of the unfit.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Pension System is a defined contribution scheme.
2. The Old Pension Scheme is a defined benefit scheme.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the National Pension System is a defined contribution scheme in which the benefit depends on the accumulated corpus, while the Old Pension Scheme is a defined benefit scheme guaranteeing a fixed pension.

q: Leave on Average Pay is credited in advance to the leave account of a railway servant in two instalments of 15 days each, falling due on:
e: Leave on Average Pay is credited in advance to the leave account in two instalments of 15 days each, falling due on 1st January and 1st July of every year.

q: A railway servant availing Leave Travel Concession (LTC) may encash Leave on Average Pay at his credit, at a time, up to:
e: A railway servant availing Leave Travel Concession may encash Leave on Average Pay at his credit up to a maximum of 10 days at a time.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Casual leave is not a recognised kind of leave under the Leave Rules and is not debited to the leave account of a railway servant.
2. Casual leave can be combined with any other kind of leave.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: casual leave is not a recognised kind of leave and is not debited to the leave account. Statement 2 is wrong: casual leave cannot be combined with any other kind of leave. Hence 1 only.

q: Which of the following statements regarding leave of a railway servant is correct?

options.A: Leave can be claimed as a matter of right in all circumstances
options.B: Leave applied for must invariably be granted by the sanctioning authority
options.C: Leave once sanctioned can never be curtailed or revoked
options.D: Leave cannot be claimed as a matter of right and may be refused or revoked by the sanctioning authority in the exigencies of public service

e: Leave cannot be claimed as a matter of right; it may be refused, curtailed or revoked by the sanctioning authority in the exigencies of public service.

q: Joining time is NOT admissible to a railway servant when the transfer is:

options.D: Made between two offices of the same Railway in public interest

e: Joining time is admissible only on transfer in public interest; it is not admissible when the transfer is made at the railway servant's own request.

q: Child Care Leave is admissible to a female railway servant for taking care of her two eldest surviving children up to the age of:
e: Child Care Leave is admissible to a female railway servant for taking care of her two eldest surviving children up to the age of 18 years.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Maternity leave is not debited to the leave account of the female railway servant.
2. Full leave salary is payable during maternity leave.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: maternity leave is not debited to the leave account of the female railway servant, and full leave salary is payable during the period of such leave.

q: The maximum period for which Special Disability Leave can be granted to a railway servant in his entire service is:
e: Special Disability Leave, granted for injury or disability sustained in the discharge of official duty, can be granted for a maximum period of 24 months in the entire service.

q: In which record is every step in the official life of a non-gazetted railway servant recorded?
e: Every step in the official life of a non-gazetted railway servant, including appointments, promotions, leave and punishments, is recorded in his Service Book.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Leave on Half Average Pay can be granted on medical certificate as well as on private affairs
options.B: Commuted leave can be granted on private affairs
options.C: Leave on Half Average Pay can be granted only on production of a medical certificate
options.D: Commuted leave does not require a medical certificate

e: Inspection and acceptance of the work by the Railway do not relieve the contractor of his responsibility for the quality and soundness of the work; liability for defects remains with him.

q: A period of absence which is treated as 'dies non' means that:

options.A: Full salary is payable for the period
options.B: The period counts for increment but not for pension
options.C: Half salary is payable for the period
options.D: No salary is payable for the period and it counts neither for increment nor for pension

e: Dies non means the period of absence is treated as not spent on duty: no salary is payable for it and it counts neither for increment nor for pension.

q: Under the 7th CPC pay structure, the two dates on which annual increment is granted are:

options.C: 1st January and the date of appointment
options.D: 1st July and the date of promotion

e: Under the 7th CPC pay structure, annual increments are granted only on two dates, 1st January and 1st July, depending on the date of appointment, promotion or financial upgradation.

q: The annual increment under the 7th CPC pay matrix is granted at the rate of:

options.A: 2% of the pay in the level
options.B: 2.5% of the pay in the level
options.C: 3% of the pay in the level
options.D: 5% of the pay in the level

e: The annual increment under the 7th CPC pay matrix is granted at the rate of 3% of the pay in the level, and the pay then moves to the next cell of the same level.

q: On promotion of a railway servant, his pay in the higher level is fixed:

options.A: At the same cell as in the lower level in all cases
options.B: By granting one increment in the lower level and then fixing the pay at a cell in the higher level equal to or next above the amount so arrived at
options.C: At the minimum of the higher level in all cases
options.D: By granting two increments in the lower level invariably

e: On promotion, pay is fixed by granting one increment in the lower level and then fixing the pay in the higher level at a cell equal to or next above the amount so arrived at.

q: A railway servant who has reached the maximum of his pay level becomes eligible for a stagnation increment after every:
e: A railway servant who has reached the maximum of his pay level becomes eligible for a stagnation increment, equal to one increment, after every two years.

q: A railway servant whose date of birth is 1st June will retire from service on attaining the age of superannuation on the:
e: Retirement takes effect on the afternoon of the last day of the month of superannuation; a servant born on 1st June is deemed to attain the retirement age a day earlier, so he retires on the afternoon of 31st May.

q: In the context of railway establishment bills, the abbreviation IPAS stands for:
e: In railway establishment bills, IPAS stands for Integrated Payroll and Accounting System, the application through which pay bills and establishment accounting are processed.

q: On the transfer of a railway servant, the document issued by the transferring office showing the last pay drawn and the recoveries outstanding against him is the:
e: The Last Pay Certificate issued by the transferring office shows the last pay drawn by the railway servant and the recoveries outstanding against him, so that the new office can continue his payments correctly.

q: The minimum qualifying service required for a railway servant to become eligible for pension on superannuation is:
e: The minimum qualifying service required for a railway servant to become eligible for pension on superannuation is 10 years.

q: A railway servant retiring after completing full qualifying service is entitled to pension equal to:

options.C: 50% of the last pay drawn (or average emoluments, whichever is more beneficial)

e: A railway servant retiring after completing full qualifying service is entitled to pension equal to 50% of the last pay drawn or of the average emoluments, whichever is more beneficial to him.

q: A railway pensioner becomes entitled to additional quantum of pension at the rate of 20% of the basic pension on attaining the age of:
e: Additional quantum of pension begins at the rate of 20% of the basic pension on attaining the age of 80 years, and rises further at the higher age slabs.

q: Family pension at the normal rate is payable at:
e: Family pension at the normal rate is payable at 30% of the last pay drawn by the deceased railway servant, as against 50% at the enhanced rate.

q: The portion of pension commuted by a railway pensioner is restored to him after a period of:

options.A: 15 years from the date of commutation
options.B: 10 years from the date of commutation
options.C: 12 years from the date of retirement

e: The portion of pension commuted by a pensioner is restored to him after the expiry of 15 years from the date of commutation.

q: Retirement gratuity admissible to a railway servant is calculated at the rate of:

options.A: Half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, subject to a maximum of 33 times the emoluments
options.B: One month's emoluments for each completed year of qualifying service
options.C: One-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, subject to a maximum of 16½ times the emoluments
options.D: 15 days' emoluments for each completed year of qualifying service

e: Retirement gratuity is calculated at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, subject to a maximum of 16.5 times the emoluments.

q: Where a railway servant dies in service after rendering 20 years or more of qualifying service, death gratuity is payable at the rate of:

options.A: One-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period, subject to a maximum of 16½ times the emoluments
options.B: 12 times the emoluments in all cases
options.C: One month's emoluments for each completed year of service
options.D: Half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, subject to a maximum of 33 times the emoluments

e: Where a railway servant dies in service after 20 years or more of qualifying service, death gratuity is payable at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, subject to a maximum of 33 times the emoluments.

q: On superannuation, an NPS subscriber is required to utilise the accumulated pension wealth for purchase of an annuity to the extent of at least:
e: On superannuation, an NPS subscriber is required to utilise at least 40% of the accumulated pension wealth for the purchase of an annuity to provide a regular pension.

q: Partial withdrawal from the NPS Tier-I account of a subscriber is permissible up to:
e: Partial withdrawal from the NPS Tier-I account is permissible up to 25% of the subscriber's own contribution, for specified purposes such as children's education or marriage and treatment of specified illnesses.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), the minimum assured payout on superannuation after a minimum qualifying service of 10 years is:
e: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the minimum assured payout on superannuation after the minimum qualifying service of 10 years is Rs 10,000 per month.

q: A railway servant may seek voluntary retirement after completion of:
e: A railway servant may seek voluntary retirement after completion of 20 years of qualifying service, subject to giving the prescribed notice and its acceptance by the competent authority.

q: The post-check of pension paid through banks is carried out in the Accounts Office on the basis of:

options.B: The monthly scrolls received from the pension-paying banks
options.C: The ticket stubs received from stations
options.D: The muster rolls of the pensioners

e: The post-check of pension paid through banks is carried out in the Accounts Office on the basis of the monthly scrolls received from the pension-paying banks, which show the amounts actually disbursed.

q: The minimum subscription to the Provident Fund payable by a railway servant is:
e: The minimum subscription to the Provident Fund payable by a railway servant is 6% of his emoluments, though he may subscribe a higher amount voluntarily.

q: A temporary (refundable) advance sanctioned from the Provident Fund is ordinarily recovered in monthly instalments not exceeding:
e: A temporary (refundable) advance sanctioned from the Provident Fund is ordinarily recovered in monthly instalments not exceeding 36, along with continued regular subscription.

q: An appeal against an order imposing a penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules must be preferred within a period of:

options.A: 30 days from the date of the order
options.B: 15 days from the date of the order
options.C: 60 days from the date of the order
options.D: 45 days from the date on which the order is delivered to the appellant

e: An appeal against an order imposing a penalty must be preferred within 45 days from the date on which a copy of the order is delivered to the appellant.

q: Unless extended after review by the competent authority, an order of suspension ceases to be valid after a period of:
e: Unless extended after review by the competent authority, an order of suspension ceases to be valid after a period of 90 days.

q: In a departmental inquiry, the Presenting Officer is appointed to:

options.A: Assist the charged railway servant in presenting his defence
options.B: Record the proceedings on behalf of the inquiry officer
options.C: Present the case in support of the charges on behalf of the disciplinary authority
options.D: Decide the penalty to be imposed on the charged official

e: In a departmental inquiry, the Presenting Officer is appointed to present the case in support of the charges on behalf of the disciplinary authority before the Inquiry Officer.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A charged railway servant may take the assistance of another railway servant (serving or retired) or an office bearer of a recognised trade union as his defence assistant.
2. A legal practitioner can be engaged as defence assistant as a matter of right in every departmental inquiry.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: the charged servant may take the assistance of another railway servant, serving or retired, or an office bearer of a recognised trade union. Statement 2 is wrong: a legal practitioner can be engaged only with permission, not as a matter of right. Hence 1 only.

q: A post created to accommodate a particular incumbent personally, which is not a part of the regular cadre and lapses as soon as it is vacated, is known as a/an:
e: A supernumerary post is created personally to accommodate a particular incumbent, is not part of the regular cadre, and lapses as soon as it is vacated by him.

q: A post which is borne outside the cadre of the service to which the incumbent belongs is called a/an:
e: An ex-cadre post is a post borne outside the cadre of the service to which the incumbent belongs, whereas a cadre post forms part of that cadre itself.

q: A post whose pay is charged to the cost of a specific work or estimate is called a:
e: A work-charged post is one whose pay is charged to the cost of a specific work or estimate, rather than to the regular revenue establishment.

q: The periodical check exercised in the Accounts Office to ensure that the number of staff actually borne and paid does not exceed the sanctioned strength is known as:
e: Scale Check is the periodical check exercised in the Accounts Office to ensure that the number of staff actually borne and paid does not exceed the sanctioned strength in each scale.

q: Non-selection posts on the Railways are filled:

options.A: By a positive act of selection on the basis of merit alone
options.B: By nomination of the controlling officer
options.C: On the basis of seniority subject to rejection of the unfit

e: Non-selection posts are filled on the basis of seniority subject to rejection of the unfit, without any positive act of selection on merit.

q: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, Children Education Allowance is reimbursed at the rate of:
e: Children Education Allowance is now Rs 2,812.50 per month per child. (Source: DoPT OM No. A-27012/01/2023-Pers.Policy(Allowance) dated 25.04.2024; effective 01.01.2024.)

q: In regard to House Rent Allowance, the correct position is that:

options.A: HRA is admissible at full rates even when a railway servant occupies a railway quarter
options.B: HRA is not admissible to a railway servant who is provided with railway accommodation
options.C: HRA is admissible at 50% of the normal rate when a railway quarter is occupied
options.D: HRA has been abolished under the 7th CPC

e: House Rent Allowance is not admissible to a railway servant who is provided with railway accommodation, since HRA is meant to compensate only those not provided with Government housing.

q: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations (HOER), the standard rostered hours of work for staff classified as 'Continuous' are:
e: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, the standard rostered hours of work for staff classified as 'Continuous' are 48 hours per week.

q: Running Allowance admissible to running staff such as Loco Pilots and Guards is paid on the basis of:

options.A: The number of hours of duty performed
options.B: A flat rate per month irrespective of the work done
options.C: The number of trains worked during the month
options.D: The kilometreage performed by the staff

e: Running Allowance admissible to running staff such as Loco Pilots and Guards is paid on the basis of the kilometreage performed by them during the month.

q: Maternity leave granted to a female railway servant:

options.A: Cannot be combined with any other kind of leave
options.B: May be combined with any other kind of leave due and admissible to her
options.C: Can be combined only with casual leave
options.D: Must always be availed in continuation of Child Care Leave

e: Maternity leave may be combined with any other kind of leave due and admissible to the female railway servant, including leave on medical grounds.

q: A railway servant prefixes and suffixes holidays to a spell of leave. The correct position is:

options.A: The holidays so prefixed/suffixed are not treated as part of the leave
options.B: Holidays can never be prefixed to a spell of leave
options.C: The holidays are debited to the leave account of the railway servant
options.D: Only one holiday, either as prefix or as suffix, is permissible

e: Holidays prefixed or suffixed to a spell of leave are not treated as part of the leave and are therefore not debited to the leave account of the railway servant.

q: Leave salary payable during a period of commuted leave is:

options.A: Half of the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay
options.B: 75% of the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay
options.C: The same as the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.D: Nil, as commuted leave is without leave salary

e: Leave salary during commuted leave is the same as the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay, because the commuted leave is paid at the full average-pay rate against double debit of LHAP.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Extra Ordinary Leave granted on medical certificate counts for increment.
2. Extra Ordinary Leave granted otherwise than on medical certificate does not count for increment, and the date of the next increment is postponed to the extent of such leave.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: EOL granted on medical certificate counts for increment, while EOL granted on other grounds does not count and the date of the next increment is postponed to the extent of such leave.

q: Extra Ordinary Leave granted to a railway servant otherwise than on medical certificate is treated, for pension purposes, as:

options.A: Counting in full as qualifying service
options.B: Counting to the extent of half the period of leave
options.C: Counting only if the leave exceeds one year

e: Extra Ordinary Leave granted otherwise than on medical certificate does not count as qualifying service for pension.

q: Study leave granted to a railway servant is:

options.A: Debited against his Leave on Average Pay account
options.B: Debited against his Leave on Half Average Pay account
options.C: Not debited to his leave account
options.D: Treated as dies non for the period of the course

e: Study leave is a separate kind of leave granted for prosecuting a course of study; it is not debited to the Leave on Average Pay or the Leave on Half Average Pay account of the railway servant.

q: Hospital leave is admissible to a railway servant:

options.A: For any illness, whether or not connected with his official duty
options.B: Only when he is admitted to a railway hospital for a surgical operation
options.C: Only if he belongs to the running staff categories
options.D: Belonging to specified categories exposed to risk of accident or injury, when the illness or injury is directly attributable to the discharge of his official duty

e: Hospital leave is admissible only to specified categories of railway servants exposed to risk of accident or injury, and only when the illness or injury is directly attributable to the discharge of their official duty.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Quarantine leave is not debited to the leave account of a railway servant.
2. Quarantine leave is ordinarily granted for a period not exceeding 21 days at a time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: quarantine leave, granted when a member of the servant's family suffers from an infectious disease, is not debited to the leave account and is ordinarily granted for a period not exceeding 21 days at a time.

q: Special Casual Leave admissible to a male railway servant for undergoing sterilisation operation is:
e: Special Casual Leave admissible to a male railway servant for undergoing sterilisation operation is 6 working days.

q: Joining time granted to a railway servant on transfer in public interest is:

options.A: Debited to his Leave on Average Pay account
options.C: Admissible only to gazetted railway servants
options.D: Treated as duty for all purposes and is not debited to the leave account

e: Joining time granted on transfer in public interest is treated as duty for all purposes, including pay, and is not debited to the leave account of the railway servant.

q: If, at the time of retirement, the Leave on Average Pay at the credit of a railway servant is less than 300 days, leave encashment is admissible as under:

options.A: Encashment is confined to the Leave on Average Pay at credit only
options.B: Leave on Half Average Pay cannot be encashed in any circumstances
options.C: Encashment is restricted to a maximum of 150 days in all cases
options.D: The shortfall in Leave on Average Pay can be made good by encashment of Leave on Half Average Pay at his credit, so that the total encashment does not exceed 300 days

e: If the LAP at credit at retirement is less than 300 days, the shortfall can be made good by encashment of LHAP at his credit, so that the total encashment of leave does not exceed 300 days.

q: At the time of retirement, a railway servant has 250 days of Leave on Average Pay and 120 days of Leave on Half Average Pay at his credit. The maximum total number of days for which leave encashment is admissible to him is:
e: LAP at credit is 250 days; the shortfall against the 300-day ceiling is 300 - 250 = 50 days, which alone can be made good from the 120 days of LHAP. Total encashment is thus capped at 300 days, not 370 days.

q: A railway servant dies while in service. The cash equivalent of leave admissible to his family is:

options.A: Cash equivalent of the Leave on Average Pay standing at his credit, subject to a maximum of 300 days
options.B: Cash equivalent of 150 days of Leave on Average Pay only
options.C: No leave encashment is payable to the family on death in service
options.D: Cash equivalent of the entire leave at his credit, without any ceiling

e: On the death of a railway servant in service, his family is paid the cash equivalent of the Leave on Average Pay standing at his credit, subject to a maximum of 300 days.

q: A railway servant, on promotion, opts to have his pay fixed from the date of his next increment in the lower post. The effect of this option is that:

options.A: He forfeits the benefit of one increment permanently
options.B: His pay is fixed at the minimum of the higher level from the date of promotion
options.C: He gets only the annual increment, and not the promotion increment, on that date
options.D: On that date he gets the benefit of two increments — the annual increment and the promotion increment — and his pay is then fixed in the higher level

e: Where a railway servant opts for pay fixation from the date of his next increment in the lower post, on that date he gets two increments - the annual increment and the promotion increment - and his pay is then fixed in the higher level.

q: A railway servant is promoted to a higher level with effect from 15th March, 2026 and his pay is fixed from the date of promotion. He will be entitled to his next increment on:
e: Promoted on 15th March 2026 with pay fixed from the date of promotion, he has not completed the required period of service in the higher level by 1st July 2026, so his next increment falls due on 1st January 2027.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding stepping up of pay:
1. The senior and the junior railway servants must belong to the same cadre, and the posts held by them in the lower as well as the higher level must be identical.
2. The anomaly in the pay of the senior must have arisen directly as a result of fixation of pay on promotion under FR 22.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both conditions must hold for stepping up: the senior and junior must belong to the same cadre with identical posts in the lower and higher levels, and the anomaly must arise directly from fixation of pay on promotion under FR 22.

q: A railway servant proceeding on deputation to an ex-cadre post draws his pay as under:

options.A: He must draw only the pay of the ex-cadre post
options.B: He must draw only the pay of his parent cadre post
options.C: He may opt either for the pay of the ex-cadre post or for the pay of his parent cadre post plus deputation (duty) allowance
options.D: He draws the lower of the pay of the two posts

e: A railway servant on deputation to an ex-cadre post may opt either for the pay of the ex-cadre post or for the pay of his parent cadre post plus deputation (duty) allowance.

q: A railway servant is transferred, at his own request, to a post carrying a lower scale of pay. His pay in the lower post cannot exceed:

options.A: His substantive pay in the higher post
options.B: The maximum of the scale of pay of the lower post
options.C: His officiating pay in the higher post
options.D: The average pay of the lower scale

e: Where a railway servant is transferred at his own request to a post carrying a lower scale of pay, his pay in the lower post cannot exceed the maximum of the scale of pay of that post.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) scheme:
1. MACP confers only a financial upgradation; there is no change in the designation or the seniority of the railway servant.
2. Grant of financial upgradation under MACP is treated as a regular promotion for all purposes, including seniority in the higher grade.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: MACP confers only a financial upgradation, with no change in designation or seniority. Statement 2 is wrong: MACP upgradation is not treated as a regular promotion for seniority and other purposes. Hence 1 only.

q: On grant of a financial upgradation under the MACP scheme, the pay of a railway servant is fixed:

options.A: At the minimum of the next level in all cases
options.B: By granting one increment in the existing level and fixing the pay at a cell equal to or next above the amount so arrived at in the higher level, as on promotion
options.C: By granting two increments in the existing level
options.D: Without any increment; only the level of pay changes

e: On grant of financial upgradation under MACP, pay is fixed by granting one increment in the existing level and then fixing the pay at a cell equal to or next above that amount in the higher level, exactly as on promotion.

q: An interruption (break) in the service of a railway servant entails:

options.A: No consequence for the purpose of pension
options.B: Forfeiture of half of his past service for pension
options.C: Only postponement of his next increment
options.D: Forfeiture of his past service for pension, unless the break is condoned by the competent authority

e: An interruption or break in service entails forfeiture of the railway servant's past service for pension, unless the break is condoned by the competent authority.

q: Qualifying service for the purpose of pension of a railway servant commences from the date on which he attains the age of:
e: Qualifying service for pension commences from the date on which the railway servant attains the age of 18 years; service rendered before that age does not count.

q: Family pension at the enhanced rate is payable, in the case of death of a railway servant in service, for a period of:

options.A: 5 years, or till the deceased would have attained the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
options.B: 7 years, or till the deceased would have attained the age of 67 years, whichever is earlier
options.C: 10 years in all cases, irrespective of age
options.D: 7 years, or till the deceased would have attained the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier

e: On death in service, family pension at the enhanced rate (50% of last pay) is now payable for 10 years from the date of death; the 7-year / age-67 limit applies only to death after retirement. (Source: CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, Rule 50(2)(a)(ii), DoPPW; PIB release dated 23.09.2019; effective 01.10.2019.)

q: A railway servant who seeks voluntary retirement from service is required to give a notice of not less than:
e: A railway servant seeking voluntary retirement is required to give a notice of not less than 3 months to the appointing authority.

q: Where the period of suspension of a railway servant is prolonged beyond three months for reasons not directly attributable to him, his subsistence allowance for the remaining period may be increased by an amount not exceeding:

options.A: 25% of the subsistence allowance admissible during the first three months
options.B: 50% of the subsistence allowance admissible during the first three months
options.C: 75% of the subsistence allowance admissible during the first three months
options.D: 100% of the subsistence allowance admissible during the first three months

e: Where suspension is prolonged beyond three months for reasons not directly attributable to the railway servant, his subsistence allowance may be increased by an amount not exceeding 50% of the subsistence allowance admissible during the first three months.
